strings.name: Lesetja Kganyago
strings.role: Governor of the South African Reserve Bank; Chancellor of Stellenbosch University
strings.summary: Lesetja Kganyago is a South African economist and central banker who previously served as National Treasury Director-General and Reserve Bank Deputy Governor, becoming Governor in 2014. He works in monetary policy, financial stability and international financial governance and also holds Stellenbosch University's ceremonial chancellorship. His public policy arguments distinguish the roles of price stability, institutional trust and structural reform.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Distinguishes current and former offices, appointment announcements and effective dates, inflation targets and actual outcomes, and payment reform plans and completed measures.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads the South African Reserve Bank and participates in emerging-market monetary policy and international financial governance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Holds a BCom in accounting and economics from the University of South Africa and an MSc in development economics from SOAS, University of London; honorary doctorates are distinguished from these degrees.
strings.facts.f2.label: Governor's term
strings.facts.f2.value: His third five-year term began on November 9, 2024 and is scheduled to end on November 8, 2029; the latter is not an already completed term.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Fiscal and monetary policy experience
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from the National Treasury into central bank leadership and formerly chaired the International Monetary and Financial Committee, which advises the IMF Board of Governors on policy.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Policy boundaries between stability and growth
strings.highlights.h2.text: In a 2026 speech, argued that price stability provides a foundation for growth but cannot replace reforms to infrastructure, productivity and public institutions; these are his policy assessments.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Delivers an awards address
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed public trust, transparency and central bank accountability at the Sunday Times awards event in Johannesburg.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Outlines payment system reform
strings.timeline.t2.text: Discussed non-bank access and interoperability at the central bank's payments conference; subsequent frameworks and pilots remained plans.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Installed as university Chancellor
strings.timeline.t3.text: Formally installed as Stellenbosch University's 16th Chancellor after election on January 24; the office primarily performs ceremonial duties.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Begins third term as Governor
strings.timeline.t4.text: Reappointed Governor of the South African Reserve Bank, starting another five-year term.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes IMFC Chair
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began a three-year term ending January 17, 2021; this was not the position of IMF Managing Director.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes Reserve Bank Governor
strings.timeline.t6.text: Promoted from Deputy Governor, distinct from the earlier appointment announcement date.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Moves to Deputy Governor role
strings.timeline.t7.text: Left the National Treasury Director-General position to become Deputy Governor of the South African Reserve Bank.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes National Treasury Director-General
strings.timeline.t8.text: A 2011 government statement confirms service as Director-General from this month, correcting some biographies' description as Deputy Director-General.
